_comment: What stands in a province's town. Engine data, not a campaign's: every realm raises the same set. 'room' is the scene under scene/campaign-map that the building opens; a building without one is named and described but not built yet. 'site' names the industry a building belongs to, and a province with no capacity for that industry has no such site — there is no quarry in a province with no stone in the ground, and the town shows none. 'scale' is how tall it stands, as a fraction of the picture — a keep is not a cow pen. 'spot' is where it stands on assets/city/town.png, in that picture's own proportions. Everything is kept off the edges of the picture: a wall goes round the town, and a mine drawn out where the gate will be is a mine outside its own walls, so the same fractions hold whatever the window is shaped like. The art for each one is assets/city/buildings/<key>.png, and a building with none drawn yet stands as a sign alone.

buildings.name: Keep
buildings.blurb: The seat of the province, and the walls the rest of it shelters behind.

buildings.name: Market
buildings.blurb: Buy what the land will not give you; sell what it gives too much of.

buildings.name: Blacksmith
buildings.blurb: Iron and wood into arms, a commission at a time.

buildings.name: Barracks
buildings.blurb: Men out of the province's own people, armed out of its armoury.

buildings.name: Fields
buildings.blurb: What the province eats, and what is left over to sell.

buildings.name: Pasture
buildings.blurb: Meat on the hoof. Slower than grain, and worth more at the gate.

buildings.name: Lumber Camp
buildings.blurb: Every wall, shaft and bow stave in the province starts in this yard.

buildings.name: Quarry
buildings.blurb: Cut stone, for the walls that timber will no longer answer for.

buildings.name: Mine
buildings.blurb: Ore out of the hill, and the arms and hinges it is beaten into.
